item.title: Medicaid Fraud, ICE Riots & Biden’s Secret Gender Plan: Inside DW’s Award-Worthy Investigations
item.description:
Outrageous Medicaid fraud in Ohio, a 78-page Biden administration plan to push gender ideology into child welfare agencies, and an embed with ICE agents in Minneapolis at the height of the unrest. Three investigations, three Dao Prize nominations, and the reporters who broke them.
On this episode of Behind the Story, Tim Rice sits down with Daily Wire senior investigative reporter Luke Rosiak, investigative reporter Meg Brock, and immigration reporter Jenny Taer to peel back the curtain on their intensive, change-making investigations. 
They discuss how each story came together, why the mainstream press keeps turning a blind eye to important stories like these, where citizen journalism helps and where it falls short, and what they’ll be digging into as divided government returns to Washington next year.

item.title: America, China, and the Tech Cold War with Chris Miller
item.description:
Following Trump's return from his summit in China, Jon is joined by Chris Miller, author of "Chip War: The Fight for the World's Most Critical Technology." Together, they explore the supply chain for semiconductors that runs through Taiwan, discuss how the trade war between the US and China is reshaping technology development and production, and consider what this competition reveals about the emerging world order. Plus, Jon has to choose between Nixon and Trump!

item.title: Is There an A.I. Bubble? A Debate.
item.description:
The gargantuan bet on the future of A.I. is driving the U.S. stock market and economic growth. And the building of data centers is sucking up so many construction resources, it’s crowding out the construction of homes.
The multitrillion-dollar question is: Will this bet pay off? Or is it a bubble, destined to burst and pull the economy down with it?
Paul Kedrosky is a partner at SK Ventures, a fellow at M.I.T., and the author of a newsletter about A.I.. He thinks we’re very obviously in a bubble. Azeem Azhar is a technology entrepreneur and the author of the newsletter Exponential View. He has a more optimistic take.
(The New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft claiming copyright infringement. The companies have denied those claims.)
[Journalism Quality Filter — Quality: 8/10 — Expert debate clearly explains a major economic question with competing arguments and evidence about AI investment risks.]
